gap_rows.title: Outbound egress infrastructure: endpoint names, accounts, folders, receiver ranges, PGP key identifiers, staging names, file-size limit, transfer timeout and rotation period not specified in any source
gap_rows.source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 16, 32 and 35; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-052 and NFR-053; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T5.1; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3; RWB-PLT-N012-INF
gap_rows.section: §3 Preconditions, §6 INVEST check, §8 Business rules, §10 Authority, §11 Data, §13 Solution plan
gap_rows.description: One combined row for the infrastructure values of this key. Architecture v5 slides 8, 11, 16 and 32 name the two outbound interfaces (INT-14 WIN registered mail and INT-25 debt buyers), the MFT/SFTP transport with PGP for a party outside the bank and a claim-check link for one file for 15 minutes, and slides 11 and 35 require private access, workload identity and keys in the key store; no source names the endpoint hosts, ports, accounts, folders, file patterns per environment, the receiver ranges, the PGP key identifiers or fingerprints, the staging location names, the maximum file size, the transfer timeout, the connection and read timeouts, the concurrent transfer limit or the rotation period. The 15 minutes of Architecture v5 slide 11 is the validity of the claim-check link and not a transfer budget, so it cannot be used as the timeout.
gap_rows.evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Transport: Blob + MFT/SFTP; PGP for outside parties' and 'Identity: SAS link, one file, 15 minutes' with no size or timeout value; Architecture v5 slide 35 lists zero trust and private access without naming a range; NFR-052 'Secrets are held in the key store and never in code, configuration files or prompts' without a rotation period; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3 'The SFTP outbound folders exist in DEV and SIT, with credentials in the key store (NFR-052)' and no folder name.
gap_rows.area: Integration (P2) outbound egress: MFT/SFTP endpoints, keys, network and budgets
gap_rows.proposed: Provision the two endpoints per environment with one receiver and one key each, hold the credentials, private keys and certificates in the key store behind the rwb-integration workload identity, apply the private DNS records and the egress allow-list, stage the file with its manifest and its sha256, and set the size, timeout and concurrency budgets as environment values. Fix every value with the bank MFT team, the network team and security, and record the rotation period in the key-rotation runbook.

asm_rows.text: The two MFT/SFTP endpoint names, hosts, ports, accounts, folders, receiver ranges, PGP key identifiers, staging names, maximum file size, transfer timeout and concurrency limit are environment values of the infrastructure story and are not fixed by any source; the story fixes their shape, the PGP and checksum rules and the rule that a size or timeout violation is a transfer failure.
asm_rows.why: Architecture v5 slides 8, 11 and 32 name the two interfaces and the MFT/SFTP transport with PGP and a 15-minute claim-check link, but no source names an endpoint, a receiver range or a budget.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 16, 32 and 35; RWB-PLT-N012-INF (standard Blob, key store and MFT/SFTP resources); legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3 (SFTP folders and the key store).
asm_rows.confirm: Bank MFT team, network team and security
asm_rows.impact: The endpoints and the budgets are set per environment without code or contract change; a missing budget would let a malformed file consume the retry ladder.

asm_rows.text: The certificate, credential and PGP key rotation interval is not fixed by any source; rotation follows the platform key-store runbook with a staged new version, a switch and the retirement of the previous version, and a transfer with an expired credential fails closed with no clear-text fallback.
asm_rows.why: NFR-052 requires secrets in the key store and NFR-053 requires encryption in transit, while no source fixes a rotation period for this interface.
asm_rows.read: Non Functional Specification v3 (NFR-052, NFR-053); Architecture v5 slides 11 and 35; RWB-PLT-N012-INF runbooks; legacy RWB-E1-007 section 3.
asm_rows.applied_in: §5 Exception paths (X2), §8 BR2, §11 Data, §13 Solution plan
asm_rows.confirm: Security and the bank MFT team
asm_rows.impact: A rotation is a runbook step and not a release; a stale key stops the transfer and never weakens it.
